title: Return-State Sweep
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ and $y$ be bit strings, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, and fix a selector bit vector, an input-head position on $y$, a return state of $M$, an output-register value, a Boolean boundary tag, an auxiliary output tape with head position $z_O$, and a bit string $L$. For every natural number $j$, starting in the corresponding return-state configuration with the first auxiliary tape storing $j$ consecutive ones followed by $L$ and its head at position $j-1$, the tabulating machine reaches after $j+1$ steps the corresponding decision-state configuration with that tape's head at position $0$; the tape contents and all other specified data are unchanged.
